title: Optimal interferometric certification of multi-photon indistinguishability
authors: Marco Robbio, Michał Oszmaniec, Nicolas J. Cerf, Ernesto Galvão, Leonardo Novo
abstract: Multiphoton indistinguishability is a key resource for photonic quantum technologies, yet its characterization typically relies on resource-intensive methods. In this work, we develop two efficient and experimentally friendly protocols to estimate or bound the fidelity $F_{\mathrm{ind}}$ of an $N$-photon state to the closest perfectly indistinguishable state. The first protocol applies to sources preparing separable states, uses a single Fourier interferometer together with photon-number-resolving detection, and yields tight two-sided bounds on $F_{\mathrm{ind}}$. The second protocol combines randomized implementations of linear-optical interferometers with photon counting, enabling direct estimation of $F_{\mathrm{ind}}$ for arbitrary $N$-photon states. Both protocols can certify $F_{\mathrm{ind}} = 1 - \mathcal{O}(ε)$ using provably optimal $\mathcal{O}(1/ε)$ samples, in contrast to previous approaches which required prior assumptions on the model of partial distinguishability. Our methods, based on a multiphoton generalization of the Hong-Ou-Mandel test, bring the rigorous and operationally meaningful certification of multiphoton indistinguishability within reach of current photonic technologies.
summary: This paper introduces two novel, efficient protocols to certify the indistinguishability fidelity of multi-photon quantum states. These methods generalize the Hong-Ou-Mandel effect and provide provably optimal sampling complexity for estimating this crucial resource. The development makes high-fidelity characterization of photonic quantum states accessible to current experimental technologies.
main_problem: The paper develops efficient and experimentally friendly protocols to estimate or bound the fidelity of an N-photon state to the closest perfectly indistinguishable state.
main_result: Two protocols are presented: one for separable states using a Fourier interferometer, and a randomized one for arbitrary states, both achieving optimal sample scaling of O(1/epsilon).
method: The methods generalize the Hong-Ou-Mandel test by developing protocols based on photon-number measurements and randomized linear-optical interferometers.
model_or_system: The system involves N photons in an interferometer setting, characterized by the fidelity F_ind, which measures how close the state is to perfect indistinguishability.
key_observables: Fidelity to the closest indistinguishable state (F_ind), the reduced external state (Omega_ext(rho)), and various expectation values derived from interferometry.
important_parameters: The required sample complexity scales optimally as O(1/epsilon) for certification.
main_assumptions: The protocols are designed to be operationally motivated and experimentally practical, overcoming limitations of previous methods that required strong structural assumptions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the certification problem, showing the geometric representation and detailing the setups for both the cyclic (fixed Fourier interferometer) and randomized (sampling random permutations) protocols.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical definition of indistinguishability fidelity, then details the two distinct measurement protocols (cyclic and randomized) to bound or estimate this fidelity, culminating in complexity analysis showing optimal scaling.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, operationally meaningful methods to quantify a fundamental resource (indistinguishability) in photonic quantum information, directly applicable to quantum communication and computation.
